context.requirement_text: Third and last requirement of this batch's DLQ half -- the route layer atop REQ-176's core and REQ-177's landing sites. dlq.zig (337 lines) was catalogued in docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md's fronting-subsystem table as deferred to S6 rather than built in S4; this requirement is that deferral being paid off. CONTRACT SOURCE: since R-Co's dlq.zig itself is not inspectable from this drafting session (R-Co unreachable, stated once at this batch's top and restated here rather than silently assumed covered), this requirement's binding contract is the ALREADY-SHIPPED SPA consumer: web/src/api/dlq.ts's `dlqApi` object and web/src/types/api.ts's `DlqEntry` / `CursorPage<T>` types (S8, committed, currently calling routes that 404). Build exactly to that, not a guess: GET /api/v1/dlq -- query params status, source_type (maps to entry_type), search, cursor, page_size, instance_id (dlqApi.list); response `{items: [DlqEntry], next_cursor}`. GET /api/v1/dlq/:id -- a single DlqEntry. POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry -- calls REQ-176's retry/2, returns the updated DlqEntry. POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/discard -- calls REQ-176's discard/2, returns the updated DlqEntry. AUTHORIZATION: every route requires the DlqOperate permission. REQ-069's Letflow.Api.Authorization matrix already ported DlqOperate as "currently unreachable" precisely because no S4 route consumed it yet -- this route is what makes it reachable; do not invent a new permission name. Tenant scoping follows REQ-072's cross-tenant-404 mechanism: a real id belonging to another tenant returns 404, never 403 (REQ-069's own INV-5 rule, restated for this route). web/src/pages/dlq/DlqPage.tsx's client-side OPERATE_ROLES (PROCESS_OPERATOR, PLATFORM_ADMIN) is what currently gates the retry/discard buttons in the UI -- verify which roles actually hold DlqOperate against REQ-069's real matrix rather than assuming these two are the complete server-side answer. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-176/177's context module; this is the route/controller layer only.

task.description: Validate lib/letflow/design/req178-dlq-routes.md as a hard gate before ELIXIR-DEV implements it. Read the design artefact independently -- do not treat CODE-DESIGNER's summary as evidence. For each acceptance criterion below, confirm it maps to a concrete, unambiguous design element (route/handler, function signature or call description, error-mapping table, or explicitly-flagged open question) -- no 'TBD' or silent deferral. Confirm the design contains NO implementation code: no fenced .ex/.exs code blocks, no literal function bodies, no verbatim-copied existing Elixir source reproduced in a fence -- prose/tables/pseudocode-in-prose only. Confirm function signatures/call shapes are fully specified (module, function, arity, input, the exhaustive set of output tuples/atoms). Confirm error-handling shape is explicit for every route (403/404/409/422/400 mapped to a distinct cause, not left implicit). Confirm cross-module dependencies are listed (Letflow.Dlq, Letflow.Api.Authorization, Letflow.Api.AuthorizedRouter, Letflow.Api.Pagination, Letflow.Api.Response, Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline). Confirm open questions (§7 of the design: has_more key, unmapped optional DlqEntry fields, 404-vs-400 for :invalid_id) are stated as open questions, not silently resolved by omission.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/dlq returns a body shaped exactly {items: [...], next_cursor: string|null}, and each item's field names (id, entry_type, instance_id, reason, full_reason, retry_count, status, created_at at minimum) match DlqEntry's, verified against web/src/types/api.ts rather than a hand-invented shape
GET /api/v1/dlq honors status, source_type, search, cursor and page_size independently, each with its own test demonstrating the filter narrows the result set

POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard both require the DlqOperate permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller holding no role with that permission receives 403, and a caller from a different tenant naming a real id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403 -- three explicit tests

POST /api/v1/dlq/:id/retry and .../discard against a non-existent id return 404, and against an id already "resolved" or "discarded" return a 409-shaped conflict rather than a generic 500 -- covering the not-found and terminal-state cases each with their own test

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's dlq.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that web/src/api/dlq.ts / web/src/types/api.ts were the binding contract instead, so a future reader does not assume R-Co parity was verified when it wasn't
